1	# Rayon
2	
3	[![Rayon crate](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rayon.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rayon)

6	[![build status](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon/workflows/main/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon/actions)
7	
8	Rayon is a data-parallelism library for Rust. It is extremely
9	lightweight and makes it easy to convert a sequential computation into
10	a parallel one. It also guarantees data-race freedom. (You may also
11	enjoy [this blog post][blog] about Rayon, which gives more background
12	and details about how it works, or [this video][video], from the Rust
13	Belt Rust conference.) Rayon is
14	[available on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/rayon), and
15	[API documentation is available on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rayon).
16	
17	[blog]: https://smallcultfollowing.com/babysteps/blog/2015/12/18/rayon-data-parallelism-in-rust/
18	[video]: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gof_OEv71Aw
19	
20	## Parallel iterators and more
21	
22	Rayon makes it drop-dead simple to convert sequential iterators into
23	parallel ones: usually, you just change your `foo.iter()` call into
24	`foo.par_iter()`, and Rayon does the rest:
25	
26	```rust
27	use rayon::prelude::*;
28	fn sum_of_squares(input: &[i32]) -> i32 {
29	    input.par_iter() // <-- just change that!
30	         .map(|&i| i * i)
31	         .sum()
32	}
33	```
34	
35	[Parallel iterators] take care of deciding how to divide your data
36	into tasks; it will dynamically adapt for maximum performance. If you
37	need more flexibility than that, Rayon also offers the [join] and
38	[scope] functions, which let you create parallel tasks on your own.
39	For even more control, you can create [custom thread pools] rather than
40	using Rayon's default, global thread pool.
41	
42	[Parallel iterators]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/iter/index.html
43	[join]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/fn.join.html
44	[scope]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/fn.scope.html
45	[custom thread pools]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/struct.ThreadPool.html
46	
47	## No data races
48	
49	You may have heard that parallel execution can produce all kinds of
50	crazy bugs. Well, rest easy. Rayon's APIs all guarantee **data-race
51	freedom**, which generally rules out most parallel bugs (though not
52	all). In other words, **if your code compiles**, it typically does the
53	same thing it did before.
54	
55	For the most part, parallel iterators in particular are guaranteed to
56	produce the same results as their sequential counterparts. One caveat:
57	If your iterator has side effects (for example, sending methods to
58	other threads through a [Rust channel] or writing to disk), those side
59	effects may occur in a different order. Note also that, in some cases,
60	parallel iterators offer alternative versions of the sequential
61	iterator methods that can have higher performance.
62	
63	[Rust channel]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/mpsc/fn.channel.html
64	
65	## Using Rayon
66	
67	[Rayon is available on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/rayon). The
68	recommended way to use it is to add a line into your Cargo.toml such
69	as:
70	
71	```toml
72	[dependencies]
73	rayon = "1.12"
74	```
75	
76	To use the parallel iterator APIs, a number of traits have to be in
77	scope. The easiest way to bring those things into scope is to use the
78	[Rayon prelude](https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/prelude/index.html). In
79	each module where you would like to use the parallel iterator APIs,
80	just add:
81	
82	```rust
83	use rayon::prelude::*;
84	```
85	
86	Rayon currently requires `rustc 1.85.0` or greater.
87	
88	### Usage with WebAssembly
89	
90	By default, when building to WebAssembly, Rayon will treat it as any
91	other platform without multithreading support and will fall back to
92	sequential iteration. This allows existing code to compile and run
93	successfully with no changes necessary, but it will run slower as it
94	will only use a single CPU core.
95	
96	You can build Rayon-based projects with proper multithreading support
97	for the Web, but you'll need an adapter and some project configuration
98	to account for differences between WebAssembly threads and threads on
99	the other platforms.
100	
101	Check out the
102	[wasm-bindgen-rayon](https://github.com/RReverser/wasm-bindgen-rayon)
103	docs for more details.
104	
105	## Contribution
106	
107	Rayon is an open source project! If you'd like to contribute to Rayon,
108	check out
109	[the list of "help wanted" issues](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22help+wanted%22).
110	These are all (or should be) issues that are suitable for getting
111	started, and they generally include a detailed set of instructions for
112	what to do. Please ask questions if anything is unclear! Also, check
113	out the
114	[Guide to Development](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon/wiki/Guide-to-Development)

116	assumed to

# Rayon

[![Rayon crate](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rayon.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rayon)
[![Rayon documentation](https://docs.rs/rayon/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/rayon)
![minimum rustc 1.85](https://img.shields.io/badge/rustc-1.85+-red.svg)
[![build status](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon/workflows/main/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rayon-rs/rayon/actions)

Rayon is a data-parallelism library for Rust. It is extremely
lightweight and makes it easy to convert a sequential computation into
a parallel one. It also guarantees data-race freedom. (You may also
enjoy [this blog post][blog] about Rayon, which gives more background
and details about how it works, or [this video][video], from the Rust
Belt Rust conference.) Rayon is
[available on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/rayon), and
[API documentation is available on docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rayon).

[blog]: https://smallcultfollowing.com/babysteps/blog/2015/12/18/rayon-data-parallelism-in-rust/
[video]: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gof_OEv71Aw

## Parallel iterators and more

Rayon makes it drop-dead simple to convert sequential iterators into
parallel ones: usually, you just change your `foo.iter()` call into
`foo.par_iter()`, and Rayon does the rest:

```rust
use rayon::prelude::*;
fn sum_of_squares(input: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    input.par_iter() // <-- just change that!
         .map(|&i| i * i)
         .sum()
}
```

[Parallel iterators] take care of deciding how to divide your data
into tasks; it will dynamically adapt for maximum performance. If you
need more flexibility than that, Rayon also offers the [join] and
[scope] functions, which let you create parallel tasks on your own.
For even more control, you can create [custom thread pools] rather than
using Rayon's default, global thread pool.

[Parallel iterators]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/iter/index.html
[join]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/fn.join.html
[scope]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/fn.scope.html
[custom thread pools]: https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/struct.ThreadPool.html

## No data races

You may have heard that parallel execution can produce all kinds of
crazy bugs. Well, rest easy. Rayon's APIs all guarantee **data-race
freedom**, which generally rules out most parallel bugs (though not
all). In other words, **if your code compiles**, it typically does the
same thing it did before.

For the most part, parallel iterators in particular are guaranteed to
produce the same results as their sequential counterparts. One caveat:
If your iterator has side effects (for example, sending methods to
other threads through a [Rust channel] or writing to disk), those side
effects may occur in a different order. Note also that, in some cases,
parallel iterators offer alternative versions of the sequential
iterator methods that can have higher performance.

## Using Rayon

[Rayon is available on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/rayon). The
recommended way to use it is to add a line into your Cargo.toml such
as:

```toml
[dependencies]
rayon = "1.12"
```

To use the parallel iterator APIs, a number of traits have to be in
scope. The easiest way to bring those things into scope is to use the
[Rayon prelude](https://docs.rs/rayon/*/rayon/prelude/index.html). In
each module where you would like to use the parallel iterator APIs,
just add:

```rust
use rayon::prelude::*;
```

Rayon currently requires `rustc 1.85.0` or greater.

### Usage with WebAssembly

By default, when building to WebAssembly, Rayon will treat it as any
other platform without multithreading support and will fall back to
sequential iteration. This allows existing code to compile and run
successfully with no changes necessary, but it will run slower as it
will only use a single CPU core.

You can build Rayon-based projects with proper multithreading support
for the Web, but you'll need an adapter and some project configuration
to account for differences between WebAssembly threads and threads on
the other platforms.

Check out the
[wasm-bindgen-rayon](https://github.com/RReverser/wasm-bindgen-rayon)
docs for more details.

input.rationale: Rayon 是 Rust 生态中最具代表性的数据并行库，仓库分为三层：上层 rayon（并行迭代器与各数据源适配）、底层 rayon-core（线程池、join/scope/spawn 与工作窃取调度）、以及 rayon-demo（基准演示）。学习路线因此设计为：先用入门单元让读者从零跑通第一个并行程序并建立仓库地图；接着按“使用者视角”学习并行迭代器的数据源、collect 与错误处理；再进入中间层剖析适配器如何通过 delegate 模式层层委托；然后深入 plumbing（Producer/Consumer/bridge）这一理解 rayon 的核心抽象；之后自顶向下进入 rayon-core，从 join 出发理解 Job/Latch/Registry/工作窃取/睡眠唤醒的完整调度链路，并学习 scope/spawn/broadcast 与自定义线程池；最后在专家层研读切片与并行排序实现，并完成自定义迭代器、自定义 Producer、性能调优与测试体系等二次开发实践。每个主题只讲一个问题，讲义间通过 depends_on 形成从使用到内核、从内核到扩展的递进路径。

data.head: ee0a00bdb1ab039e178a215ad5712fb7fa58e58f
data.rationale: Rayon 是 Rust 生态中最具代表性的数据并行库，仓库分为三层：上层 rayon（并行迭代器与各数据源适配）、底层 rayon-core（线程池、join/scope/spawn 与工作窃取调度）、以及 rayon-demo（基准演示）。学习路线因此设计为：先用入门单元让读者从零跑通第一个并行程序并建立仓库地图；接着按“使用者视角”学习并行迭代器的数据源、collect 与错误处理；再进入中间层剖析适配器如何通过 delegate 模式层层委托；然后深入 plumbing（Producer/Consumer/bridge）这一理解 rayon 的核心抽象；之后自顶向下进入 rayon-core，从 join 出发理解 Job/Latch/Registry/工作窃取/睡眠唤醒的完整调度链路，并学习 scope/spawn/broadcast 与自定义线程池；最后在专家层研读切片与并行排序实现，并完成自定义迭代器、自定义 Producer、性能调优与测试体系等二次开发实践。每个主题只讲一个问题，讲义间通过 depends_on 形成从使用到内核、从内核到扩展的递进路径。

lectures.title: par_bridge：桥接顺序迭代器
lectures.topic: 学习 ParallelBridge 如何把任意 std 迭代器（如文件行迭代器）接入并行世界，以及它用锁串行取元素带来的性能权衡与递归风险。

lectures.title: join：最小的并行原语
lectures.topic: 从 rayon-core 的 join 入手：两个闭包如何被调度，执行线程如何先做本地任务再窃取，以及 join_context 提供的额外信息。

lectures.title: Job 与 Latch：任务的底层表示
lectures.topic: 剖析任务对象 Job 与同步原语 Latch：闭包如何被装箱成 JobRef，闭包执行完毕如何通过 Latch 唤醒等待者。

learning_goals: 理解全局 registry 的惰性初始化流程

learning_goals: 理解本地弹出与远程窃取的方向差异

理解 crossbeam-deque Worker/Stealer 的分工

lectures.title: 工作窃取队列与调度循环

lectures.title: 睡眠与唤醒协议

learning_goals: 理解 scope 如何在生命周期内安全借用栈上数据

理解 in_place_scope 允许在池线程内嵌套的原因

lectures.title: scope：借用安全的作用域
lectures.topic: 学习 scope/scope_fifo/in_place_scope：如何在作用域内向池 spawn 借用栈上数据的任务，以及作用域结束时的等待语义。

learning_goals: 理解 spawn 的 'static + Send 约束来源

区分 broadcast 与 spawn_broadcast 的结果返回方式
minimal_modules: 与其他派发 API 的对比

lectures.title: broadcast：向所有线程广播

lectures.title: panic 传播与 unwind 安全
lectures.topic: 研读 unwind.rs：任务 panic 如何被捕获、跨线程传递并在调用方重新抛出，同时保证池与数据结构不被破坏。
